surface_summary: Lois Reddle, secretary to the Countess of Moron, discovers her mother was wrongfully imprisoned for murder. After a series of accidents and attempts on her life, Lois is abducted and detained in a remote farm under the care of a dubious doctor. Michael Dorn, a detective, investigates the case, uncovering a conspiracy involving the Countess and her associates to secure the Moron estate by eliminating Mary Pinder and her daughter.
accepted_facts: Mary Pinder was convicted of murder and imprisoned for life.
Lois Margeritta Reddle is Mary Pinder’s daughter and has a distinctive star-shaped scar.
The Countess of Moron employed Lois as her secretary and is involved in suspicious activities.
Michael Dorn is a detective investigating the case and protecting Lois.
inferred_conclusions: Mary Pinder was guilty of murder and deserved her sentence.
The accidents and attempts on Lois’s life were unrelated incidents.
Chesney Praye and Dr. Tappatt were innocent or merely minor accomplices.
mechanism_description: The Countess of Moron orchestrated the wrongful imprisonment of Mary Pinder by planting evidence and manipulating the trial. To prevent Lois from uncovering the truth and claiming the estate, the Countess and her accomplices Chesney Praye and Dr. Tappatt arranged for Lois to be abducted and detained in a remote farm disguised as a mental home. Attempts on Lois’s life included poisoned chocolates and dangerous accidents, all intended to eliminate her as a threat. Michael Dorn’s investigation exposed the conspiracy and led to the rescue of Lois and Mary.
delivery_path: Countess arranges for Mary Pinder’s conviction by planting cyanide and jewels.
Mary Pinder is imprisoned; her baby Lois is taken away and raised by a neighbor.
Lois discovers her true identity and is employed by the Countess as secretary.
Countess attempts to eliminate Lois through accidents and poisoned gifts.
Lois is abducted and detained at Gallows Farm under Dr. Tappatt’s care.
Michael Dorn investigates, discovers the conspiracy, and locates Gallows Farm.
Dorn rescues Lois and Mary; Countess’s plot is exposed and foiled.
outcome_result: The conspiracy is uncovered, Lois and Mary are freed, and the Countess’s schemes are defeated.

false_assumption.statement: Mary Pinder was guilty of murder and the evidence against her was conclusive.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The trial record and discovery of cyanide and jewels in her possession strongly suggested guilt. The refusal to provide information and lack of marriage certificate reinforced suspicion.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The evidence was planted by the Countess to frame Mary Pinder and remove her as a claimant to the estate. The true murderer was never identified, and Mary was innocent.

supporting_points: Lois was arrested for attempted murder of John Braime.
She was found near the scene of the butler’s injury.
Her presence at suspicious locations and association with the Countess.
Her erratic behavior and supposed delusions.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Lois was manipulated and framed by the Countess and her accomplices; she was innocent of any crime.

red_herrings.description: Michael Dorn’s persistent following of Lois and his intrusion into her room suggested he might be a threat or culprit.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Dorn was protecting Lois and investigating the conspiracy; his actions were motivated by concern and duty.

red_herrings.description: Selwyn Moron’s childish outbursts and opposition to his mother suggested he might be involved in the plot or acting suspiciously.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Selwyn was mentally weak and manipulated by his mother; he had no involvement in the crimes.

closed_circle.rationale: These individuals had access, motive, and opportunity to orchestrate the wrongful imprisonment and attempts on Lois’s life, while others were either victims or uninvolved.

discriminating_test.design: Michael Dorn reenacts the sequence of events leading to the abduction and detention of Lois and Mary, including the discovery of the electrified book safe and the timing of the poisoned chocolates. He verifies the presence and movements of the Countess, Chesney Praye, and Dr. Tappatt at critical times and locations. The test includes checking the physical evidence such as the scar, the locked rooms, and the intercepted letters.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This reenactment confirms the Countess’s orchestration of the wrongful imprisonment and attempts on Lois’s life, and the complicity of Chesney Praye and Dr. Tappatt in detaining the victims.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The reenactment must demonstrate that only the Countess and her accomplices had the opportunity and means to carry out the conspiracy, and that the physical evidence aligns with their involvement.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with detailed accounts of the key characters’ movements, the discovery of the scar, the poisoned chocolates, and the locked safe disguised as a book. The testimony of witnesses, the timeline of letters and telegrams, and the detective’s observations are all presented transparently. The false solution accusing Lois is clearly refuted by evidence accessible to the reader. The clues about the Countess’s motives and the roles of Chesney Praye and Dr. Tappatt are embedded in dialogue and narrative, allowing an attentive reader to deduce the true conspiracy.

anchors.claim: Lois Margeritta Reddle is the daughter of Mary Pinder
anchors.anchor: Lois Margeritta! Her own name! And the star-shaped burn on her arm!

anchors.claim: Mary Pinder was convicted of murder and imprisoned for life
anchors.anchor: Mary Pinder--Murder. Convicted at Hereford Assizes. Sentenced to death; commuted to penal servitude for life.

anchors.claim: Countess of Moron employs Lois as secretary
anchors.anchor: The Countess of Moron is pleased to learn that Miss Reddle will take up her duties as resident secretary

anchors.claim: Michael Dorn is a detective investigating the case
anchors.anchor: Michael Dorn had not closed his eyes for more than thirty-six hours.

anchors.claim: Countess’s safe disguised as a book with electric shock
anchors.anchor: A very good imitation, but it is less of a book than a steel box, and any person who attempts to pull it out automatically makes contact with a very powerful electric current.

anchors.claim: Poisoned chocolates sent to Lois
anchors.anchor: Of course they were poisoned. Hydrocyanic acid. Why did you think I came into your room that night to get them away?

anchors.claim: Lois is abducted and detained at Gallows Farm
anchors.anchor: Miss Reddle is at Gallows Farm, near Whitcomb in Somerset

anchors.claim: Dr. Tappatt runs an unlicensed mental home and detains victims
anchors.anchor: I don’t see why I should allow you to make a search. You have no more authority to act as a detective than I have to run a mental home.

anchors.claim: Chesney Praye demands Lois marry him to secure release
anchors.anchor: The first is that you marry me! That you marry me to-morrow.

anchors.claim: Countess offers money to Mary Pinder to leave and keep silent
anchors.anchor: I want you to take your daughter to South America. I will pay you a yearly sum, more than sufficient for your needs.

anchors.claim: Michael Dorn rescues Lois and Mary after fire
anchors.anchor: The fire had taken hold; great tongues of flame were leaping up from the roof.

anchors.claim: False accusation against Lois for attempted murder
anchors.anchor: I charge her with being concerned in the attempted murder of John Braime!

anchors.claim: Selwyn Moron is weak and dominated by his mother
anchors.anchor: He was a weakling, entirely under the domination of his mother, a quiet and harmless man with simple, almost childish, tastes.

anchors.claim: Countess’s plot to remove Mary Pinder as claimant
anchors.anchor: Lady Moron is a woman of infinite resource. Here, she thought, was an opportunity of removing for ever a possible claimant to the Moron estate.

anchors.claim: Michael Dorn’s persistence leads to exposure of conspiracy
anchors.anchor: I never make mistakes, and I have every right to be here.

anchors.claim: Lois’s scar is a key identifying mark
anchors.anchor: It was Lizzy’s faith that whenever the scar irritated, rain was in the offing.

anchors.claim: Sergeant Braime is a CID officer planted in Countess’s household
anchors.anchor: Braime is an officer of the Criminal Investigation Department, who has been in your service for six months.

anchors.claim: Countess’s son Selwyn installs microphone to spy
anchors.anchor: Somewhere in the house, probably in the drawing-room, was a concealed microphone, and too late that night he had remembered that he had not disconnected the instrument.

anchors.claim: Countess’s photograph of young officer left in Lois’s room
anchors.anchor: He was a boy I knew some many years ago.

anchors.claim: Countess’s safe-box is empty and electrified
anchors.anchor: Empty, eh? Of course, it would be. You suspected Braime, and left a little notebook around carelessly in your bedroom, in which you made reference to the Life of Washington.
